lessons.introText: The prefix dis- means "not" or "opposite of," as in "disagree," and the prefix pre- means "before," as in "preview." Say each word out loud and listen for the beginning.
lessons.decodableInstruction: Read ALOUD and circle all words with the target sound
lessons.fillTitle: A. Fill in the missing letters and say the word
lessons.sentenceTitle: C. Choose any word and form 4 sentences
decodableSentences: I disagree with my sister sometimes.
The magician made the rabbit disappear.
We need to prepare for the trip.
My little brother goes to preschool.

lessons.subtitle: SUFFIXES (-LESS, -NESS)
lessons.introText: The suffix -less means "without," as in "careless," and the suffix -ness turns a word into a feeling or state, as in "kindness." Say each word out loud and listen for the ending.
lessons.decodableInstruction: Read ALOUD and circle all words with the target sound
lessons.fillTitle: A. Fill in the missing letters and say the word
lessons.sentenceTitle: C. Choose any word and form 4 sentences
decodableSentences: Being careless can lead to accidents.
The room was full of darkness.

lessons.subtitle: SUFFIX (-MENT)
lessons.introText: The suffix -ment turns a verb into a noun, naming the result or action, as in "enjoyment" and "movement." Say each word out loud and listen for the ending.
lessons.decodableInstruction: Read ALOUD and circle all words with the target sound
lessons.fillTitle: A. Fill in the missing letters and say the word
lessons.sentenceTitle: C. Choose any word and form 4 sentences
decodableSentences: We felt great enjoyment at the park.
Please make your payment on time.
The excitement filled the whole room.

lessons.subtitle: CONTRACTIONS
lessons.introText: A contraction joins two words together and uses an apostrophe to show missing letters. Not often shortens to n't, as in "isn't" and "don't." Say each word out loud and listen for the missing letters.
lessons.decodableInstruction: Read ALOUD and circle all words with the target sound
lessons.fillTitle: A. Fill in the missing letters and say the word
lessons.sentenceTitle: C. Choose any word and form 4 sentences
decodableSentences: We won't be late for school.

lessons.subtitle: CONTRACTIONS
lessons.introText: Contractions can also join a pronoun with will, have, or am, as in "I'll," "we've," and "I'm." Say each word out loud and listen for the missing letters.

lessons.subtitle: MULTISYLLABLE WORDS (MIXED SYLLABLE TYPES)
lessons.introText: Longer words often mix different syllable types together — closed, vowel team, and consonant-le. Break each word into syllables, say each part, then blend it into the whole word.

lessons.subtitle: MULTISYLLABLE WORDS (MIXED SYLLABLE TYPES)
lessons.introText: Some longer words combine r-controlled syllables with magic-e or open syllables, as in "afternoon" and "wonderful." Break each word into syllables, say each part, then blend it into the whole word.
